tasks.short: Review financial and operational performance and choose improvement priorities.

steps.what: Retrieve financial statements, sales results and operational performance reports.
Align reporting periods, reconcile totals and calculate comparable performance measures.
Read departmental explanations and assemble the main variances and unanswered questions.

loop.input: Reconciled performance table and departmental reports with source identifiers.
loop.output: Variance brief separating measured changes, reported explanations and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Check every number against the table and every explanation against a cited passage; manager reviews.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per reporting period; unresolved claims become questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic, but departmental explanations contain varied free text.

steps.what: Challenge explanations with department heads and distinguish causes from reporting noise.
Approve improvement priorities, owners and investigation limits.

tasks.design: Scheduled jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconcile {ERP}, {CRM} and {OPS_SYSTEM} data and feed a governed {BI} dashboard. A bounded model drafts a source-linked variance brief in {DOCS}; the manager challenges causes and approves priorities recorded in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reporting periods, metric definitions and departmental narratives differ. Existing reporting features often stop at departmental boundaries.
tasks.enabler_now: Established data connectors and calculation rules handle preparation. AI-assisted coding reduces bespoke integration effort, while a bounded model handles written explanations.
tasks.still_hard: Causal interpretation, cost allocation and incomplete operational data remain difficult. Employee-level measures require GDPR controls and an EU AI Act assessment if used for AI-based performance monitoring.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a favourable metric hides service damage, deferred maintenance or an unsustainable workload.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of one operational improvement experiment.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling reports towards testing explanations and following improvement experiments. Formal spending and staffing authority does not expand automatically.

reach.task: Recommend which operational improvement deserves company investment.
reach.learn: Compare cash impact, strategic fit and opportunity cost across departments.

evidence.claim: Report summaries and data questions are available today; reliable answers depend on prepared data models.
Planning tools can draft narratives about assumptions and risks.
The digest reports a vendor case of reduced executive reporting effort, without a published measurement method.
Automating preparation does not establish the causes of performance changes or select worthwhile interventions.
AI-based staff performance monitoring is a listed high-risk use.

assumptions: The company has separate financial, sales and operational reporting sources.
The manager reviews departmental performance rather than preparing the financial accounts.
The automate prior fits preparation better than the complete task; causal judgement remains substantial.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
Build ranges describe working effort for an initial departmental rollout; formal consultation may add elapsed time.
unknowns: Which metrics have agreed definitions and accountable data owners?
Can the source systems supply reconciled data through supported exports or interfaces?
Does reporting include identifiable employee performance?
What access approvals and national employee consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which existing {BI} features can replace custom development?
Can proposed variance rules distinguish material changes from seasonal or accounting effects?
new_work: Review unsupported explanations and missing source data.
Maintain metric definitions, reconciliation rules and connectors.
Check whether selected experiments improved outcomes.
Monitor access permissions and model drafting errors.

tasks.short: Coordinate departmental production, pricing, sales and distribution decisions.

steps.what: Review demand, capacity, stock, margins and delivery exceptions.
Discuss departmental constraints, customer commitments and emerging operational problems.
Compare volume, price, capacity and distribution options.
Agree trade-offs and approve departmental priorities within delegated authority.
Send approved priorities, owners and deadlines to department heads.
Request progress updates and chase overdue departmental actions.

tasks.design: Configure a {BI} exception view over {ERP}, {CRM} and {OPS_SYSTEM}, with deterministic scenario calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. The manager approves structured priorities in {WORKFLOW}, which creates {PROJECT} actions and sends internal reminders through {CHAT}; department heads execute commercial and operational changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Departmental plans use different assumptions, and decisions disappear into meetings and messages. Cross-functional authority cannot be reduced to a routing rule.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing dashboards and work-management features cover visibility and follow-up. Small calculation services can expose trade-offs without an autonomous agent.
tasks.still_hard: Demand is uncertain, departmental incentives conflict and customer commitments can outweigh calculated margins. Scenario quality depends on explicit assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: Secure commitments across department heads and accept responsibility for service, margin and capacity trade-offs.

ambition.what: Twice-weekly decisions on cross-department capacity bottlenecks.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time requesting updates and more time resolving bottlenecks with department heads. Cross-department decisions remain within the existing delegation framework.

reach.task: Propose a company-wide choice between growth, margin and service resilience.
reach.learn: Translate operating scenarios into strategic choices and explicit risk appetite.

evidence.claim: Existing reporting tools support dashboard summaries and questions about operational data.
Scenario arithmetic, action creation and reminders can use deterministic rules; cross-department trade-offs remain managerial.
Configuring existing reporting and work-management features is a plausible starting point, subject to installed capabilities.

assumptions: Department heads manage execution and bring cross-department conflicts to the general manager.
Existing {BI} and {PROJECT} capabilities can support exception views and action tracking.
Scenario calculations use declared assumptions rather than inferred customer behaviour.
Approved priorities are entered as structured decisions, avoiding a model transcription step.
Time and build estimates cover an initial business-unit rollout, not company-wide planning replacement.
unknowns: Which pricing, capacity and service decisions can the manager approve?
Are demand, capacity and margin measures comparable across departments?
Which systems already support action ownership and reminders?
Would proposed data use introduce employee monitoring requiring consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Which operating constraints can be expressed as auditable scenario rules?
Which exception thresholds reliably surface matters needing cross-department intervention?
new_work: Maintain scenario assumptions and exception thresholds.
Keep action owners and escalation routes current.
Review stale data and unresolved departmental dependencies.
Check that reminders support follow-up without creating duplicate reporting.

tasks.short: Direct administrative work supporting product delivery and service provision.

steps.what: Review pending order paperwork, service documentation and administrative backlogs.
Read escalations and identify missing documents, dependencies and requested decisions.

loop.input: Escalation message, linked request and permitted supporting documents.
loop.output: Exception brief with request identifier, missing items, dependencies and source passages.
loop.check: Validate identifiers and document existence deterministically; manager checks ambiguous interpretations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per message; incomplete or conflicting cases enter manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Escalations describe missing paperwork and dependencies in inconsistent free text; structured requests bypass the loop.

steps.what: Allocate routine administrative requests to responsible teams.
Resolve competing priorities and approve exceptional administrative arrangements.
Copy decisions into a separate administrative tracking register.
Request completion updates and escalate overdue paperwork.

tasks.design: Configure one administrative queue in {WORKFLOW}, linked to records in {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {HELPDESK}, with ownership and deadlines visible in {PROJECT}. A bounded extraction loop prepares briefs from unstructured {EMAIL} escalations; the manager approves exceptions, while routine routing and reminders follow configured rules. The shared decision record replaces the duplicate {SPREADSHEET} register.
tasks.previous_blocker: Administrative requests cross departmental systems, and exceptions arrive in messages. A separate register compensates for missing shared ownership.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured queues, forms and reminders cover routine work. Lightweight integrations and bounded text extraction connect the remaining gaps.
tasks.still_hard: Exceptions can require service, finance or contractual judgement. GDPR access restrictions must follow the underlying records, including attachments and extracted briefs.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparently small paperwork exception creates a customer, contractual or operational problem.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time resolving recurring handoff failures with administrative supervisors. No new formal decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Recommend a shared administrative service model across departments.
reach.learn: Assess service cost, accountability, control separation and transition effort.

evidence.claim: Rules-based queues, ownership records and reminders can support routine administrative coordination.
A bounded extraction loop can prepare exception briefs, but this digest contains no documented case for this exact workflow.
Removing a duplicate register is feasible when the shared workflow provides the required record and reporting.

assumptions: The representative workflow is order and service administration; sector-specific administration will differ.
Administrative supervisors manage routine execution.
A small separate {SPREADSHEET} register currently duplicates operational decisions.
Only rule-covered requests are routed automatically; ambiguous exceptions remain with the manager.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one administrative workflow.
unknowns: Which administrative workflows actually consume the manager's time?
Does a duplicate register exist, and what reporting or retention duties does it fulfil?
Which exception decisions require finance, legal or customer approval?
Can existing request queues support cross-department ownership?
What access controls and national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which request types can use structured forms instead of text extraction?
Which existing system can hold the authoritative administrative decision record?
new_work: Review ambiguous extraction results and misrouted requests.
Maintain responsibility mappings and escalation deadlines.
Resolve missing documents and broken record links.
Review recurring exceptions for process changes.

tasks.short: Prepare staff schedules and duty allocations with supervisors, resolving coverage conflicts.

steps.what: Gather demand, staff availability, approved absences and required qualifications.
Build a draft roster in the workforce scheduling system {OTHER}.
Assign specific duties to rostered staff in the workforce scheduling system {OTHER}.
Discuss coverage conflicts, staff preferences and cross-team support with supervisors.
Approve consolidated coverage, overtime and duty allocations in the workforce scheduling system {OTHER}.
Publish approved schedules and duty assignments through the workforce scheduling system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Connect availability from {HCM}, qualifications from {LMS} and demand from {OPS_SYSTEM} to the workforce scheduling system {OTHER}. Configure deterministic coverage, qualification, working-time and preference rules to draft rosters and duties, with unresolved conflicts shown explicitly. Supervisors resolve exceptions with the manager, whose approval releases the schedule for publication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability, qualifications and demand are maintained separately. Scheduling rules and informal staffing arrangements are only partly recorded.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling modules can apply explicit constraints and approval workflows. AI-assisted coding makes missing data connections cheaper to build; no model is needed for routine allocation.
tasks.still_hard: National working-time rules, collective agreements, fairness and last-minute absences require local judgement. GDPR applies to staff data; adding AI-based task allocation or performance monitoring requires an EU AI Act assessment and applicable employee consultation.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate unpopular cover changes, recognise fatigue and balance preferences that cannot all be satisfied.

ambition.what: A cross-team cover desk for short-notice staffing gaps.

tasks.altitude: Supervisors spend less time constructing rosters; the manager focuses on unresolved cover and overtime choices. The cover desk would need an explicit mandate before reallocating staff across departments.

reach.task: Recommend a cross-department workforce resilience policy.
reach.learn: Compare minimum cover, overtime cost, employee experience and service continuity.

evidence.claim: Rules-based scheduling and constraint checks can generate draft rosters without a language model.
AI-based task allocation using personal traits or behaviour and staff performance monitoring are listed high-risk uses.
GDPR Article 22 limits solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
In the Netherlands, works-council consent provisions cover relevant working-time and employee monitoring arrangements.

assumptions: Supervisors prepare departmental schedules; the general manager handles consolidated coverage and exceptions.
The workforce scheduling system {OTHER} supports configurable deterministic rostering and duty rules.
If that capability is absent, a deterministic solver would replace configuration and require a revised build estimate.
Approved availability is used without copying medical absence details.
Time shares describe the end-to-end scheduling task, including supervisors' preparation.
Build ranges cover an initial scheduling group; consultation effort is indicative and formal processes may take longer.
unknowns: Which scheduling capabilities and interfaces are already licensed?
Which national rules, collective agreements and employee representation arrangements apply?
Are qualification, availability and preference records reliable?
Who can approve overtime and cross-team deployment?
How frequently do schedules change after publication?
research_questions: Can the configured scheduler explain infeasible coverage and every rule violation?
Can a shadow rollout meet coverage rules while preserving an agreed distribution of unpopular shifts?
new_work: Maintain working-time, qualification and coverage constraints.
Review infeasible schedules and last-minute staffing exceptions.
Handle employee corrections and schedule objections.
Maintain data access, consultation records and integration checks.

role.altitude: The manager's week centres on explaining performance, settling departmental trade-offs and resolving consequential exceptions. Preparation, routine routing and follow-up shrink; wider spending or staffing rights still require explicit delegation.
reach: Chief executive: turn operating evidence into investment recommendations.
Chief executive: propose shared service and workforce resilience policies.
skills_to_grow: Workforce fairness and national employment rules
role.ambitious_version: Lead a weekly operating improvement cycle that selects experiments, checks outcomes and brings evidence-backed investment choices to the chief executive.
